expectations.text: hunts.md separates indicator-based queries (domains, IP, hash) from behaviour-based queries and labels which is which
expectations.evidence: H01 is headed 'IOC sweep across all XDR device tables' with 'Detection potential: LOW / IOC-only'; the legend defines 'LOW / IOC-only — hunt now, then push to indicators'. Sub-queries are labelled '5a - exact IOC plus any file in that folder' vs '5b - generic', '6a - connections to IOC infrastructure' vs '6d - behavioural'; H02 is called 'the report's strongest behavioural signal'; the promotion matrix groups 'H01, H03, H05a, H05c, H06a-c, H07a-d, H08 | Hash / domains / IP / task name / path'. Separation is per query rather than by section, but every query is labelled.

expectations.text: No behaviour query matches the full sample command line verbatim or relies solely on sample-specific strings (the task name 'OneDrive Sync Health', 'upd.exe', the fictional hash) — behaviour queries anchor on the process (conhost/powershell/schtasks via FileName) and a few invariant tokens such as --headless, irm/iex, /create with an AppData\Roaming path
expectations.evidence: H02: 'InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "conhost.exe" and InitiatingProcessCommandLine has "--headless"', 'FileName in~ ("powershell.exe", "pwsh.exe", ...)', HasCradle on irm/iwr/iex/downloadstring tokens. H04a: 'FileName =~ "schtasks.exe" and ProcessCommandLine has_any ("/create", "/change")' with '\AppData\Roaming\' regex; the task name is an additive 'or ... has ioc_taskname', not the sole anchor. H05b/H09 are generic (script host writes PE into Roaming; chained signals). 'FileName =~ "upd.exe"' appears only in 5a/5c, which are labelled IOC/'covered by indicators'.

expectations.text: IOC values are declared once (let dynamic list or externaldata) and bound to appropriate columns and operators: domains with has_any on RemoteUrl/Url-type columns, the IP with in/== on RemoteIP
expectations.evidence: Override of auto-grade (which only checked that lets exist). The shared block declares 'let ioc_domains = dynamic([...]); let ioc_ips = dynamic(["203.0.113.45"]);' and H06a binds them correctly ('RemoteIP in (ioc_ips) or RemoteUrl has_any (ioc_domains)'), but the same values are re-typed as literals in three queries: 6b line 366 'Answers has "203.0.113.45"' (ioc_ips not declared in that block), 7b lines 436/447/448/455 '_Im_WebSession(... url_has_any=dynamic(["cdn-updates-check.com", "telemetry-sync-cloud.net"]))', '_Im_Dns(... response_has_any_prefix=dynamic(["203.0.113.45"]))', and 7c line 465 'Name has_any ("cdn-updates-check.com", "telemetry-sync-cloud.net") or IPAddresses has "203.0.113.45"'. The pack's own rotation advice ('replace the let ioc_* = dynamic([...]) lines with _GetWatchlist') would therefore miss three queries. 'Declared once' is not met.

SHA256 in (ioc_sha256) or RemoteIP in (ioc_ips) or RemoteUrl has_any (ioc_domains) or FolderPath has @"\AppData\Roaming\msbuild\" | join kind=inner (AlertInfo | project AlertId, Title, Severity, Category, DetectionSource) on AlertId' under 'Also check whether Defender already alerted on any of it'.

expectations.text: Every KQL query in hunts.md is time-bounded (ago(), between, or Sentinel {{StartTimeISO}} placeholders)
expectations.evidence: Override of auto-grade. It flagged one unbounded block, the 'Shared IOC block' at line 24, which contains only let statements (no table reference) and is not a query; it also carries 'let lookback = 30d;'. Every real query is bounded: 'Timestamp > ago(lookback)' (H01-H06, H08-H10a), 'TimeGenerated > ago(90d)' (H04c, H07a, 7c, 7d), '_Im_*(starttime=ago(90d), endtime=now())' (7b), 'ago(14d)' (H10b), 'ago(30d)' (baseline). Verified by independent fence extraction: 27/27 table-bearing blocks bounded.

claims.claim: KQL blocks are plausibly valid Advanced Hunting KQL
claims.evidence: Lint: 0 errors. Real columns throughout (FileOriginUrl/FileOriginIP, RemoteIPType, UrlClickEvents.IsClickedThrough, EmailUrlInfo.UrlDomain, ThreatIntelligenceIndicator fields); FileProfile() invoked after a summarize with the documented 1000 cap; union-of-lets in H01 is well formed. 'has "--headless"' and regex extracts with doubled quotes inside @"..." strings are syntactically fine.

claims.claim: Pack is usable today: clear run order, no placeholders left unfilled
claims.evidence: Run order is explicit (section 0, H01→H02→H04/H05→H06/H07→H09→H10). But H10b ships 'let affected_users = dynamic(["user1@contoso.com", "user2@contoso.com"])' and 'Location !in ("GB", "DE", "FR", "NL") // adjust to your countries' (lint W014); it is labelled 'replace the list with H09 output' but is an unfilled placeholder. Every other query is self-contained with its own let lines.

claims.claim: 'XDR custom detections ... the queries above already carry them [Timestamp, DeviceId, ReportId]'
claims.evidence: True for H02 and H04/H05 single-event queries; false for H09 (the self-declared best rule candidate), whose output is 'summarize ... by DeviceId, DeviceName, bin(T, window)' with no Timestamp or ReportId, and for H06d/H05b (FileProfile-enriched aggregates). The parenthetical 'drop the summarize steps or re-add those columns' is the only mitigation.

claims.claim: 'The report's hash is explicitly fictional/placeholder and will differ per build'
claims.evidence: Partially right but misses the real defect: the value is 65 hex characters, not a valid SHA256 length, so the H01/H05a/H07d hash clauses can never match regardless of build. Not noticed.

claims.claim: 'There is no ASR rule that blocks conhost.exe --headless -> powershell.exe directly'
claims.evidence: Consistent with the published ASR rule set (no parent/child conhost rule exists); cannot be re-verified from outputs alone.

suggestions.assertion: IOC values are declared once (let dynamic list or externaldata) and bound to appropriate columns and operators: domains with has_any on RemoteUrl/Url-type columns, the IP with in/== on RemoteIP
suggestions.reason: The pre-grade passes on 'IOC lets: True' as soon as any let dynamic exists. Run B declares the lets and then re-types the domains/IP as inline literals in 6b, 7b, 7c (lines 366, 436, 447-448, 455, 465), so a rotation would miss three queries. Check that each IOC literal appears only inside a let declaration (or watchlist/externaldata), not scattered through queries.

suggestions.assertion: Every KQL query in hunts.md is time-bounded (ago(), between, or Sentinel {{StartTimeISO}} placeholders)
suggestions.reason: The machine pre-grade treats every ```kql fence as a query, so a let-only IOC block (B, C) counts as 'unbounded', and its fence tracking breaks on the ```yaml block in C (it reported a block starting '--- ## 4.'). More importantly the assertion has no stated position on XDR custom-detection drafts, which legitimately omit a Timestamp filter because the platform owns the lookback: A satisfied it with ingestion_time() > ago(4h), C omitted the bound and explained why. State whether a detection draft must still carry ago()/ingestion_time() or is exempt.

suggestions.assertion: Each query carries a MITRE ATT&CK mapping that names the behaviour (e.g. T1204.004 or T1204.002, T1059.001, T1053.005, T1071.001, T1041/T1567), not a generic placeholder
suggestions.reason: 'Each query' cannot be met literally by a vendor-alert sweep (AlertEvidence/SecurityAlert) or a preflight/coverage query; A and C mark those with a dash and a reason. Clarify that hunt queries over raw telemetry need a mapping and alert/preflight queries are exempt, otherwise graders will split on it.

The report's SHA256 is 65 hex characters (verified with wc -c), so any hash sweep built from it can never match. Only run C noticed; A and B shipped hash clauses and A even annotated it 'MDE stores hashes lower-case'. If the malformed hash is deliberate, add an assertion for noticing it; if accidental, fix the fixture, because it silently invalidates the hash IOC in every pack.

eval_feedback.overall: Run B fails 3/11: inline IOC literals outside the let block, four hunts with no MITRE mapping, and two uncapped make_set calls caught by the linter. The machine pre-grades for 3 and 8 were both wrong in opposite directions and had to be overridden.
